section: Later Vedic society - four varnas, ashrama system, gotra, decline in the status of women

accepted.s: In the context of later Vedic society, the institution of gotra denoted descent from a common male ancestor and was established during the
accepted.x: Gotra as an institution based on descent from a common male ancestor was established in the Later Vedic period.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the period of institutional development from the first textual occurrence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the terms Kula, Vamsha and Gotra, respectively?
accepted.x: Kula means family or household, Vamsha means lineage or dynasty, and Gotra means an exogamous clan.
accepted.tq: Match each technical term with its precise social meaning.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out in relation to ancient Indian kinship terminology?
accepted.x: Kula, Vamsha and Gotra are kinship terms, whereas Kosa means treasury.
accepted.tq: Identify the term that belongs to a different conceptual group.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding gotra rules:
1. Gotra exogamy prohibited marriage within the same gotra.
2. Caste endogamy operated along with gotra exogamy in the North Indian pattern.
3. Sapinda prohibitions were associated with the sasan rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Gotra exogamy prohibited intra-gotra marriage, while caste endogamy and sapinda restrictions formed additional elements of the North Indian kinship pattern.
accepted.tq: Combine a basic rule with its associated social restrictions.

accepted.s: Who analysed sapinda and gotra rules and divided India into four kinship zones in the work titled Kinship Organization in India?
accepted.x: Irawati Karve analysed sapinda and gotra rules and divided India into four kinship zones in Kinship Organization in India, published in 1953.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work association as the deciding clue.

accepted.s: The term ‘gotra’ literally means
accepted.x: Gotra literally means ‘cow-pen’ and later came to denote lineage from a common male ancestor.
accepted.tq: Test the literal meaning of a technical term rather than its later institutional meaning.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Upanayana is correct?
o: It was a marriage ceremony available only to women of the Brahmana varna.
It was an initiation into Vedic study and was restricted to the upper three varnas.
It marked entry into guild membership for Vaishyas.
It was a funeral rite performed for all four varnas.
accepted.x: Upanayana was the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study and was available to the Brahmana, Kshatriya and Vaishya varnas, but not to Shudras and women.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition and eligibility rule to distinguish the correct social practice.

accepted.s: The elaborate description of the Upanayana ceremony is found in the
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana gives an elaborate description of the Upanayana ceremony.
accepted.tq: Use the text–ritual association and avoid swapping closely related Vedic works.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Varna)
a. Brahmana
b. Kshatriya
c. Vaishya

a. List-II (Upanayana metre)
i. Jagati
ii. Gayatri
iii. Trishtubh

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The Brahmana Upanayana was associated with Gayatri, the Kshatriya with Trishtubh, and the Vaishya with Jagati.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure varna–metre pair and eliminate incompatible codes.

accepted.s: In the gurukula system of education, the pupil generally
o: lived separately from the teacher and studied independently
received instruction only from guild heads
accepted.x: In the gurukula system, pupils lived with the guru. Education was confined largely to the Dvija communities.
accepted.tq: Test the defining institutional feature of the education system.

accepted.s: Which of the following samskaras was associated with tonsure in the third year?
accepted.x: Chudakarma was the tonsure ceremony, traditionally performed in the third year.
accepted.tq: Associate each rite with its specific purpose or stage of life.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Garbhadhana — Conception
2. Pumsavana — Procuring a male child
3. Simantonnayana — Safety of the child in the womb
4. Jatakarma — Ceremony at birth before cutting the cord
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These samskaras relate respectively to conception, procuring a male child, protection in the womb and the birth ceremony before cutting the cord.
accepted.tq: Check each purpose independently before selecting the comprehensive combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a samskara with its significance?
o: Upanayana — entry into Vedic study and status as a Dvija
Vivaha — tonsure in the third year
Jatakarma — procurement of a male child
accepted.x: Upanayana marked entry into Vedic study and conferred Dvija status. Vivaha means marriage, Jatakarma is the birth ceremony, and Garbhadhana concerns conception.
accepted.tq: Use the elimination method by separating rites of education, birth, marriage and conception.

accepted.s: The number of samskaras traditionally recognised in this context is
accepted.x: The traditional total number of samskaras is sixteen.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact numerical value from the ritual classification.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Purusharthas?
accepted.x: The four Purusharthas are Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha. Karma is an important related concept but is not one of the four goals in this classification.
accepted.tq: Find the familiar related term that does not belong to the official fourfold list.

accepted.s: The term ‘trivarga’ refers to
accepted.x: Trivarga comprises Dharma, Artha and Kama, the first three Purusharthas. Moksha was added later as the fourth goal.
accepted.tq: Separate the older threefold classification from the later fourfold formulation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence in which the four Purusharthas developed?
o: Moksha was first, followed by Dharma, Artha and Kama
Dharma, Artha and Kama formed the earlier trivarga, while Moksha was added later
Artha and Kama were added after Moksha in the Upanishadic period
All four developed simultaneously in the early Vedic period
accepted.x: Dharma, Artha and Kama formed the earlier trivarga in the Later Vedic-Sutra phase. Moksha was added later under Upanishadic ideas of karma, samsara and liberation.
accepted.tq: Identify the earlier core and the later addition rather than treating the list as simultaneous.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Purushartha)
a. Dharma
b. Artha
c. Kama
d. Moksha

List-II (Meaning)
i. Liberation
ii. Desire
iii. Duty
iv. Wealth

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: Dharma means duty, Artha wealth, Kama desire and Moksha liberation.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive pair Moksha–liberation and complete the remaining matches.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the status of women in the Later Vedic period:
1. Women lost the right of Upanayana.
2. Women’s participation in religious rites and assemblies became restricted.
3. Women’s education became more widely available than in the Rig Vedic period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The status of women declined through loss of Upanayana, restricted education and exclusion from several religious and public activities; education did not become more widely available.
accepted.tq: Detect the reversed trend in the statement about women’s education.

accepted.s: Which Vedic text mentions that a daughter was a source of misery while a son was the protector?
accepted.x: The Aitareya Brahmana presents the daughter as a source of misery and the son as the protector, reflecting the declining status of women.
accepted.tq: Use the text-specific reference instead of confusing it with another passage on women.

accepted.s: The Maitrayani Samhita lists which of the following as three evils?
accepted.x: The Maitrayani Samhita lists liquor, dice and women as three evils.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-member list without substituting related social practices.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding women in Later Vedic society?
o: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad prohibited women from philosophical debate.
The Shatapatha Brahmana described the wife as half of her husband and as completing him.
Women universally retained Upanayana and unrestricted access to assemblies.
Gargi and Maitreyi were excluded from higher learning.
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana states that the wife is half of her husband and completes him. Gargi and Maitreyi illustrate that some women nevertheless received higher learning.
accepted.tq: Separate the general decline in status from important textual and individual exceptions.

accepted.s: Gargi’s philosophical debate with Yajnavalkya is recorded in the
accepted.x: Gargi debated Yajnavalkya in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad. Maitreyi, also associated with Yajnavalkya, is another example of a woman philosopher.
accepted.tq: Apply the person–text association and avoid swapping neighbouring Vedic works.

accepted.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the Later Vedic family structure?
o: Joint family and rising paternal authority, including the father’s power to disinherit a son
Replacement of the family by guild-based households
Decline of paternal authority and abolition of the joint family
Equal inheritance authority for all members of the household
accepted.x: The Later Vedic period witnessed the joint family and rising paternal authority; the father could even disinherit a son.
accepted.tq: Identify the social consequence that fits the described family structure.

accepted.s: References to which of the following practices appear in accounts of the declining status of women in Later Vedic society?
o: Compulsory female military service and polyandry
Abolition of marriage and communal ownership
Female kingship and universal widow remarriage
accepted.x: References to child marriage and sati appear in accounts of the declining status of women in Later Vedic society.
accepted.tq: Select the pair of practices directly associated with the stated social trend.

accepted.s: The Iron Age economy was associated with
o: the replacement of trade by ritual exchange
accepted.x: The Iron Age economy brought specialised crafts. Vaishyas worked as farmers, traders and artisans and paid tribute.
accepted.tq: Link the economic change to its principal occupational consequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following occupations were associated with the Vaishyas in Later Vedic society?
accepted.x: Vaishyas engaged in farming, trade and craft production and paid tribute.
accepted.tq: Use the occupational cluster rather than selecting a single profession.

accepted.s: The first reference to money-lending in the Vedic literature is found in the
accepted.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana contains the first reference to money-lending.
accepted.tq: Match the economic practice with the specific textual source.

accepted.s: In later Vedic texts, the guild-like body of Vaishyas was known as a gana and was headed by a
accepted.x: A gana was a guild-like body of Vaishyas, and its head was called a Shreshthin.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the occupational organisation from the titles of teachers and household authorities.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Shreshthin — head of a Vaishya gana
Shatapatha Brahmana — first reference to money-lending
Upadhyaya — head of a Vaishya gana
accepted.x: Upadhyaya was a teacher who taught the Veda or Vedanga for a livelihood, not the head of a Vaishya gana. The head of such a body was the Shreshthin.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped occupational title among otherwise familiar associations.

accepted.s: The Chandala is described as a despised birth in the
accepted.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad contains an early reference to the Chandala as a despised birth.
accepted.tq: Match the social category with the precise textual reference.

accepted.s: Which statement best distinguishes discrimination in Later Vedic society from the later formalisation of untouchability?
o: Untouchability was fully formalised in the Rig Veda and disappeared in the Dharmasutras.
Discrimination against Shudras and Chandalas existed in Later Vedic society, while untouchability as a formal rule belonged to the post-Vedic Dharmasutras.
The Dharmasutras abolished all distinctions between Shudras and Chandalas.
Discrimination against Shudras began only during the Gupta period.
accepted.x: Later Vedic society witnessed discrimination against Shudras and Chandalas, but untouchability as a formal rule is associated with the post-Vedic Dharmasutras.
accepted.tq: Separate an early social practice from its later formal legal-religious formulation.
